Static guards on integration-nightly.yml (#1896), the CI home for the live-instance root suite (~93 files needing a running Trinity; nothing ran them, so they gated nothing). Pins the properties whose absence is invisible until the night it matters: membership is DIRECTORY-based (--ignore=unit, matching tests/run-core.sh) so #1895's relocations shrink it with no workflow edit and no file list to drift; base and head both run for attribution; a missing JUnit fails the job LOUDLY instead of being reported to the author as a regression (the diff script is fail-closed on missing XML, so a failed stack boot would otherwise wear a PR's name — #1941's class); each side gets a pristine stack via `down -v` since the suite mutates its instance; the merge is full-depth with the conflict verdict gated on unmerged paths (#1941 again); the job running untrusted PR code holds only contents:read while the write-scoped comment job never checks out PR code; it is not on the pull_request path; the runtime budget and its escalation are written down; --continue-on-collection-errors is present (measured: 3 root modules currently fail to import, and without the flag pytest writes no XML at all); and src/cli is installed, since test_cli_*.py imports trinity_cli which is deliberately absent from requirements-test.txt.

Static guard on backend-unit-nightly.yml's merge check (#1941). The job shallow-fetched both dev and the PR head, so the merge had no common ancestor and git's `refusing to merge unrelated histories` was recorded as `merge_conflict=true` for EVERY open PR (9/9, 8 of them MERGEABLE) — the detector's output was independent of its input, so the suite never ran and the regression signal defaulted to clean. Asserts: base checkout is fetch-depth 0; the pull/N/head fetch carries no --depth; the merge_conflict=true branch is gated on actual unmerged paths (--diff-filter=U) so an infrastructure failure can't be reported as a PR conflict; --allow-unrelated-histories is never used (it would fabricate a merge of unrelated trees and run the suite against a worktree that isn't the real merge result); and the `git merge dev` advice stays inside the conflict/regression branches. Comment lines are stripped before matching — the fix's own comment says 'no --depth' and a naive substring search matches it and passes while the command is shallow again.

Enabling the audit hash chain set an instance attribute and wrote nothing, and nothing restored it at boot - so every backend restart silently switched the integrity control back off, with restarts being routine (CLAUDE.md documents re-login after one). An install could sit unhashed indefinitely while the feature still showed as available, and #1985's verified_partial reports valid:true for a range that is mostly unverifiable. The chain HEAD had the same defect one level down: self._last_hash made the chain a property of one PROCESS, so with >1 worker each kept its own head and wrote previous_hash values pointing into another worker's sequence - verify_chain's link check then reported an untampered log as TAMPERED, the loud false positive its own docstring warns against. Fix: the flag persists in system_settings and resolves live per write (uncached, per the _resolve_bool_flag rationale, but fail-CLOSED rather than fail-open since it decides whether an integrity record is written), and db.create_audit_entry_chained reads the head inside the INSERT's own transaction. Covers restart survival both directions, default-off, two instances over one store agreeing (the --workers 2 relationship), live-not-cached, nine stored-value parsings, fail-closed on a settings error, a pin that neither _hash_chain_enabled nor _last_hash exists on the instance, the chained-vs-plain writer choice, an end-to-end two-instance interleaved append verifying as ONE valid chain, and the retention consumer that gated on the old private attribute via getattr(...,False) - a default that would have degraded silently to 'never warn'. The atomicity guard walks the AST and requires the SELECT and the INSERT to be in the same with-block with no head read outside it: an earlier substring-on-ast.dump version passed when the read was hoisted out. Mutation-verified: flag back in the instance (6 fail), fail-open (1), always-plain-writer (2), head read in a separate transaction (1).

Single-owner git env derivation across both container-rebuild paths (ent#109 PR 1). recreate_container_with_updated_config seeds env from the OLD container and re-derived only GITHUB_PAT, replaying whatever GITHUB_REPO / GIT_SYNC_* each container carried; its one production caller is start_agent_internal, fired by nine config-drift predicates AND base-image drift at cold start, so a base-image rebuild arms that replay fleet-wide. 22 tests over the 1484-shape purge-and-mock harness (copied from test_ent123_tokenless_clone, deliberately not shared - sys.modules leaks). (1) PAT gate is a REQUIRED per-call-site parameter: the ent#162 regression verbatim - a tokenless agent plus a configured GLOBAL platform PAT must NOT get GITHUB_PAT under pat_gate='per_agent_only' (a verbatim lift would have swapped #211's per-agent gate for the 2-tier per-agent->global resolver, configure_push_remote clears the push blackhole, and Cornelius can push a private KB to the shared public upstream) - plus the contrast case proving pat_gate='effective' DOES resolve it (so the assertion is the gate's doing, not a dead resolver), the per-agent-row and already-tokened-container arms, an unknown gate rejected, and an AST static guard pinning the WRITER SET, not just the two known sites: `{recreate_container_with_updated_config: per_agent_only, _apply_persisted_auth_env: effective}` exactly, so a THIRD writer on any container-seeded path fails CI (ent#109's bug WAS that git env had two writers and one was wrong; the earlier source-grep version stayed green through a planted third `effective` writer - proved by mutation). The AST also fails loud on a non-literal `pat_gate`, which would make the guard vacuous, and ignores the module's two prose mentions of the helper that a substring count read as writers (the #1871 guard's own first blind spot). (2) GIT_SYNC_AUTO = DB flag OR baked env, DERIVE-ONLY: baked-true/DB-0 keeps auto-push (crud.py's two writers genuinely disagree - 'and not config.ephemeral' sits inside a swallowing try/except on the DB side only, column default 0 - so DB-only derivation silently stops auto-push for that slice of the fleet), but the column is NEVER written back: 'baked true / DB 0' is ALSO exactly what an owner's explicit PUT /{agent}/git/auto-sync {enabled:false} looks like (that endpoint writes the row and nothing else, while the agent gates on container env), so a backfill would re-enable the flag, erase the only record of the intent, and cross a privilege boundary - PUT .../auto-sync is OwnedAgentByName while POST .../start, which triggers the recreate, is AuthorizedAgentByName, and an agent-scoped key resolves to its owner carrying the owner's role (trinity-ops-agent#232). DB-only enables; neither source clears a stale flag. (2b) Correct, never introduce, on the config-drift path: the block is repo-gated while the PAT is per-agent-gated, and those two disagree for an agent bound post-creation via POST /{agent}/git/initialize on the GLOBAL platform PAT (no baked git env, no per-agent PAT row, credential only in .git/config, not covered by startup.sh's #1264 .env fallback) - introducing GIT_SYNC_ENABLED=true with no GITHUB_PAT makes the restart branch rewrite origin to the credential-less CLONE_URL and configure_push_remote blackhole the push remote, silently and fleet-wide on the same base-image drift this fix exists for. So per_agent_only writes the block only when the old container already carried GITHUB_REPO or a PAT resolves; a carried repo is still corrected; effective is exempt (no old container - not introducing there is the #843/#1439 silently-empty-agent bug); the no-row clear sweep is unaffected. (3) Set-or-clear: a deleted agent_git_config row pops every var in _GIT_ENV_KEYS from a carried-forward dict and touches nothing else, a source_mode flip clears the mode/branch pair, TRINITY_GIT_BASE_URL refreshes from the CURRENT backend env, the owned key set is complete, and the one deliberate divergence from a verbatim lift is asserted (a container with a baked PAT and NO git binding loses it rather than having it refreshed from the global platform PAT - the per-agent PAT is a column ON that row). (4) Idempotence: two passes produce an identical env dict and the DB row is never mutated, so the writer can never feed a config-drift matcher into an infinite recreate loop. Every one of the four behaviours was proved to have teeth by mutation (un-gate the PAT, flip the call site to 'effective', derive GIT_SYNC_AUTO DB-only, drop the clear sweep, drop the source-mode clear, diverge the GIT_SYNC_AUTO literal, restore the DB backfill, remove the introduce-guard: all eight go red). No Docker, no backend, no Redis.

Post-creation repo binding engine (ent#109 PR 2). Classification refuses every unsupported shape BY NAME and partitions on source_mode (the column idx_git_config_repo_branch_unique keys on) rather than on write credentials, which is orthogonal: a credential-less source_mode=0 row would pass a credentials gate and be rebound INSIDE that index. An already-writable agent is an ORDINARY rebind, and trinity-system is refused through the no-git-config path so it never reaches a container recreate. The CAS is the commit point: a row that moved yields 409 with nothing partial, and the post-commit loser is RESTORED to captured previous values, never deleted (delete_git_config on a pre-existing row strips a live agent's binding so its next recreate drops GITHUB_REPO -- #843/#1439). Ordering: the PAT is persisted after the rewire and strictly before the recreate. Resumption (review C1): the fixture tracks the container's origin INDEPENDENTLY of the DB row, because that divergence is the whole subject -- deriving one from the other made the retry regression test pass against code that refused the retry with BIND_STATE_UNCLASSIFIED. Both post-commit shapes are covered: push-failed (row moved, origin did not) and recreate-failed (both name the destination, but it now holds our own pushed history, which the destination policy read as foreign data). A resume does not repoint upstream at the destination, and a row naming a THIRD repo is still unclassified. Secret hygiene: the PAT is absent from the outcome, the audit and every error path, and a stale baked token in git output is redacted too (it is not user_pat, so scrub_secret alone misses it).

The bind ENDPOINT surface (ent#109 PR 2). 422 bodies must not echo the value that failed validation (ent#109 /cso S1 follow-through). Pydantic v2 records the rejected value in errors()[i]['input'] and FastAPI's default handler returns exc.errors() verbatim, so a failed SecretStr validation returns the SECRET in the response body and in any log of it. Load-bearing rather than incidental: without error_handlers.validation_error_without_input, ent#109's PAT charset guard would RELOCATE the h11 leak from a 500 into a 422 instead of closing it. 'input' is dropped for every field rather than for names that look sensitive -- a name-matching allowlist is the new-producer-missing-from-the-consumer's-list class, and the caller already has the value they just sent. Includes a teeth test asserting FastAPI's default WOULD have leaked, so the suite fails loudly if the framework changes and the handler becomes redundant, rather than passing for an unrelated reason.

Failed-creation container reclaim (ent#313): a create that fails after containers.run must leave no orphan container, no unreclaimable volume and no name-keyed Redis state. Covers both arrival shapes — handle in hand (later step raised) and NO handle (the reported 60s Docker read timeout, where the daemon created the container and the client never got it, so it is re-derived by name). Pins every fail-closed gate on that re-derived path, because a name resolves to another install's live agent on a shared Docker daemon: 409 name conflict (daemon created nothing) → refuse; existing agent_ownership row (a concurrent creation won the name) → refuse; trinity.created label older than the attempt's floor, missing, or unparseable → refuse; missing floor → refuse; DB or Docker lookup error → refuse. Also: Redis cleared when the container is provably gone (removed or never created) and NOT when removal failed (the slot ZSET isn't idle); every failure swallowed so the original creation error is what the caller reports; and an AST guard that create_agent_internal actually AWAITS the reclaim, so the unit tests can't stay green while nothing calls it. Also pins the never-raises contract under a stubbed docker module: the first version used isinstance(exc, docker.errors.APIError), which raises TypeError wherever docker is a test double and replaced the real creation error with an unrelated one (caught by the full suite via test_fork_to_own / test_1484); the 409 check is duck-typed on .response.status_code now.

Atomic SSH-port allocation via a per-port Redis reservation (#2215 D1). `get_next_available_port()` was an unlocked check-then-act: two concurrent creators (the fresh-install seeders under `--workers 2`) read the same `trinity.ssh-port` label snapshot, computed the same `max+1`, and the second `containers.run` failed `Bind for 0.0.0.0:X failed: port is already allocated` — after which the default-system deploy latches `default_system_seeded` on a permanently-incomplete `partial`. The regression is pinned DETERMINISTICALLY, with no timing: two SEQUENTIAL calls against an UNCHANGED stubbed Docker snapshot must return DIFFERENT ports (pre-fix: the same port — the race in unit form), with a bounded threaded belt (N concurrent calls -> N distinct ports) beside it. Gate ORDER is load-bearing and pinned: the SETNX reservation is the LAST gate, after the label scan and `is_port_available`, so a host-bound candidate the scan walks past never leaves a 600s reservation behind. SETNX contention -> continue scanning (never return the contended port unreserved, which would hand out a port exactly while the race is happening); a RAISED Redis error fails OPEN with exactly one reservation attempt and the client resolved once per call. `exclude=` binds the forward scan AND the 2222-2500 fallback scan (merged once, before both loops). Every reservation carries `ex=600`: a dropped TTL would make a stale key permanently unallocatable, since no reaper exists. The label scan is STRICT — a Docker listing fault RAISES rather than degrading to `list_all_agents_fast`'s `[]`, which would compute `start_port = 2222` and confidently reserve an existing agent's port (`is_port_available` is netns-blind in production, so nothing downstream would catch it) — while demo mode (`docker_client is None`) still allocates from the base. Also pins the stated guarantee BOUNDARY: Redis-down double assignment is convergent, driven through a D2-shaped `exclude=` retry to distinct final ports. `reserve_port_for_recreate` sets WITHOUT NX (the recreating agent's own port; a stale key must never block it) and is fail-open. Harness: real modules captured at module scope and re-owned per test, `redis_breaker_util` INCLUDED — it is not on conftest's invariant list, and a leaked MagicMock makes every SETNX "succeed" and silently defeats the race tests; `is_port_available` is ALWAYS stubbed (it binds real sockets); fakeredis over hand-rolled stubs (honors nx/ex); all thread coordination bounded so a deadlock cannot hang the randomized suite.

Bounded port-bind-conflict retry in the create path plus the reclaim precedence guard (#2215 D2/D2b). The D1 reservation is fail-open, so a collision can still surface at `containers.run` — Redis down/restarted, an expired reservation, a foreign host process — and `_run_agent_container_with_port_retry` converges it within the same create call, before a first-run seed deploy computes a permanently-latched `partial`. The cross-phase theme all three plan reviewers hit independently: `_is_container_name_conflict`'s text fallback matches the bare substring "already in use", which Docker Desktop's bind failure ("… bind: address already in use") CONTAINS — but a bind conflict proves `containers.create` SUCCEEDED (the daemon holds a Created husk of OURS) while a name conflict proves it created NOTHING, so misordering them strands the husk, 409s every retry of the name, and lets Cornelius's next-boot 409-convergence burn the durable seed flag on a dead container (the #1790 latch). Pins the classifier vocabulary (narrow two-phrase bind match, the documented Desktop overlap, and disjointness where it must hold — never `isinstance` against the docker module, which may be a test double, and never the generic "conflict", so daemon-unreachable/timeout errors bubble without burning retries); the strict per-attempt ORDER (record failed port -> clean up the husk -> reallocate with `exclude=` -> retry) with cleanup on EVERY bind-classified attempt, the final one INCLUDED, so a bind husk is never handed to the generic ent#313 reclaim still on the name; and abort-on-any-cleanup-doubt (ownership row present, lookup failure, unprovable provenance, removal failure) re-raising the ORIGINAL bind error rather than the cleanup error, because proceeding after a failed removal makes the next attempt 409 against our own husk, which the reclaim then reads as "not ours" and strands. Cleanup uses a direct `containers.get`, not `get_agent_container`, whose flattening of a lookup FAILURE into "absent" would read as "safe to retry". Non-bind errors and caller-pinned ports never retry; attempts bounded at 3; exhausted retries reach the unchanged rollback + reclaim. D2b: a bind error arriving at `_reclaim_failed_creation_container` with no handle re-derives the container under the ent#313 fail-closed gates instead of declining. Wiring guards close the ship-dead failure modes: `create_agent_internal` awaits the WRAPPER (not the raw create), and `auto_allocated_port` is captured BEFORE the port mutation — captured after, the gate is always-False and the whole retry ships inert. Harness mirrors test_ent313_failed_creation_container_reclaim.py: the real crud module with its Docker/DB seams monkeypatched BY OBJECT (crud from-imports at module top, so `crud.<name>` is where the code resolves), no sys.modules writes.

A cron tick suppressed by the Redis distributed lock must leave an audit record (#1969). Suppression is correct behaviour; the evidence was missing - the lock-denial branch of _execute_schedule logged at INFO and returned bare, so no schedule_executions row was written and a denied tick was indistinguishable from a tick that never fired, while APScheduler still reported the job successful. Trinity already audited the OTHER suppression path (APScheduler max_instances -> _on_job_max_instances -> a skipped row), so this was a missing call, not a design gap. The two never overlap: a max_instances refusal means the job never started, so _execute_schedule is never entered and no lock is attempted; reaching the lock branch means APScheduler already let it start. The gap bit hardest on the common case, since a MANUAL trigger bypasses APScheduler entirely (_trigger_handler dispatches via asyncio.create_task) and its collision with the cron tick lands one layer down in exactly the unaudited branch. Covers: a denied tick records exactly one skipped row; the reason names the LOCK, not max_instances, so the two causes stay tellable apart in the record; the audited tick still does NOT run the schedule (auditing suppression must not undo it); the granted-lock path stays silent (a skipped row per successful tick would invert the status for every consumer); the pre-existing lock release survives on both the success and raise paths and no release is attempted when no lock was handed out. #91 regression shape: exactly one row per denial, three denials -> three rows, plus a source guard that the max_instances listener still never routes through _execute_schedule (which would audit one tick twice) and that the audit helper still swallows its own errors, now load-bearing because it is called from the cron execution path. Ends with an end-to-end pass against a real temp SQLite DB proving a status='skipped' row actually lands - the wiring tests alone would still pass with a broken write path.

Codex subscription auth must survive Trinity's dispatch (#1971). _execute_codex set BOTH OPENAI_API_KEY and CODEX_API_KEY from the same resolved value, described in-source as harmless defence ('some Codex builds also read CODEX_API_KEY'). It is not harmless: the mere PRESENCE of CODEX_API_KEY flips the Codex CLI into API-key auth mode and makes it discard a valid subscription auth.json, so every subscription agent 401'd against api.openai.com, retried 5x and failed the turn - while the same auth.json worked when the CLI was invoked directly. Through /task that was the only reachable behaviour. A SECOND defect is visible in the reporter's own repro but was not filed: their working case is 'only a placeholder OPENAI_API_KEY set', a placeholder because _execute_codex raised 503 before invoking the CLI whenever no API key was found - and a ChatGPT-plan container has no API key by design. Fixing only the reported half leaves subscription agents working provided they know to set a fake key. Covers: source tracking (which variable the key came from, incl. the cold-start .env parse) with an explicit guard that _load_openai_api_key remains the patchable seam _execute_codex calls - the first attempt moved it and turned 127 existing Codex tests red; subscription detection that is existence+non-empty ONLY (a zero-byte file and a directory are both rejected, but invalid JSON is accepted, because validating is the CLI's job and a stale token must surface as the CLI's auth error rather than a Trinity 503 falsely claiming no credentials); the env actually handed to the child - CODEX_API_KEY no longer synthesized from an OPENAI_API_KEY, still forwarded when the operator supplied it UNDER THAT NAME (the only case the original rationale covers), neither variable fabricated for a subscription agent, CODEX_HOME (#1098) still exported; and the gate - subscription auth alone now dispatches, no credentials at all still fails fast so the gate is not a no-op, and the 503 names BOTH remedies since the old message said only 'inject OPENAI_API_KEY' and thereby pointed subscription users at the placeholder workaround that caused this issue.

/edge-cases boundary + property analysis of the Codex credential resolvers (#1971): _parse_env_value, _load_api_key_with_source, _has_subscription_auth. These are parsing/auth boundaries whose output now decides whether CODEX_API_KEY is exported (and therefore whether a subscription auth.json survives) and whether dispatch is refused - a promotion from what _parse_env_value was originally for. 32 boundary rows (quoting, inline-comment vs in-value '#', empty/whitespace values that must not resolve to '', export prefix, missing/unreadable .env, auth.json absent/zero-byte/directory/broken-symlink) plus 4 Hypothesis properties (parse is total and never grows its input; resolution is total and self-consistent - a (value, None) or (None, source) pair would make the export decision incoherent; subscription detection is total). Found a REAL PRE-EXISTING bug, fixed here: a .env holding non-UTF-8 bytes (a Latin-1 credential, a mis-encoded smart quote - both plausible in a hand-edited file) made read_text() raise UnicodeDecodeError, which is a ValueError and NOT an OSError, so the except (IOError, OSError) around the loop never caught it; the error escaped _execute_codex and failed the dispatch instead of resolving the key or returning the honest 503. Fixed with errors='replace' so a bad byte on an unrelated line cannot hide a valid key. Also documents (not asserts as correct) that .env resolution is by LINE ORDER while the process-env branch is by _API_KEY_VARS priority - harmless while the source only chose a value, but after #1971 it also decides the auth mode. One Hypothesis finding was classified a WRONG TEST and recorded as such: lone surrogates cannot be written to a real file, so that input is unproducible.

A global GitHub PAT rotation must actually reach running agents (#1967). The #211 auto-propagation reported success while updating nothing, for two independent reasons, both caused by the global path and the per-agent path (#1264) having drifted apart. (1) The eligibility gate was .env-shaped: _propagate_to_agent passed add_if_missing=False, so an agent with no /home/developer/.env - which is EVERY agent provisioned from a GitHub template, since those ship .env.example - returned skipped_no_pat; on such a fleet 100% skipped and the endpoint still answered success:true. (2) .env is not where git authenticates from: clones are created as https://oauth2:<PAT>@github.com/... and that URL is persisted in .git/config on the workspace volume, so rewriting .env changes nothing for the running git process - only git_service.update_remote_pat restores fetch/push before a restart, and only the per-agent path called it. Observed: agents on a revoked token for 11-13 days with nothing in the UI saying so. Covers both halves: an agent with a git config but no .env is now updated (add_if_missing derived per agent, not hard-coded), and the live remote is re-templated with remotes_updated reported SEPARATELY from updated (updated alone overstates the fix - an agent whose .env was rewritten but whose remote was not is still broken for git until restart, which would repeat this issue's own mistake of reporting success for a partial effect). Critically also pins what the fix must NOT be: the issue suggests add_if_missing=True unconditionally, which would spray the global token into every running container including agents that never touched GitHub - the module docstring says the original gate existed to prevent exactly that - so eligibility moved to the git config and a non-GitHub agent keeps the conservative behaviour, with an explicit no-regression test that an agent carrying GITHUB_PAT for the gh CLI with no Trinity-managed repo is STILL rotated (the new gate is a union with the old, not a replacement). Plus: per-agent-PAT agents still skipped and never contacted, stopped agents neither counted nor contacted, one failing agent does not stop the fleet, a git-config read that raises degrades to the conservative gate instead of taking down the rotation, a zero-reach rotation WARNs in the platform log (the failure was silent for weeks; a Settings panel nobody is watching during an incident is not sufficient), and two structural guards that both paths share one _apply_pat_to_agent body and that add_if_missing=False is not reintroduced - the drift IS the bug.

An unhashed audit chain must not report as verified (#1984). POST /api/audit-log/verify answered valid:true, checked:0 for a log in which no entry carried a hash - found by probing a live instance: 1,162 real audit entries, zero hashes, green tick in the UI. valid:true was returned for three materially different states (chain verified, range empty, no integrity data at all) and the last is the DEFAULT for every install that never enabled hashing, so the verdict was independent of the input - the class learnings.md already names from #1941. Skipping an unhashed entry is correct on its own (a chain enabled midway legitimately has an unhashed prefix); the defect was the aggregate verdict when EVERY entry was skipped. valid is now tri-state: None rather than False, because False claims tampering - an equally wrong and much louder lie - while a caller doing a truthiness test degrades to 'not verified', the safe direction. Covers: rows-with-no-hashes yields unverifiable not valid; unverifiable is falsy but is NOT False and does not set first_invalid_id; empty_range is its own state (both it and no-hashes report checked:0, which was previously the only signal and made them indistinguishable); an intact chain still verifies and tampering is still detected (no regression); a partially hashed range is named verified_partial with skipped_unhashed exposed, so the permanent unhashed prefix of a late-enabled chain cannot pass for full coverage; the response reports hash_chain_enabled at all, mirroring what monitoring/status already does with enabled:false beside a stale summary; and the response model accepts a null valid (it was `bool`, which would have 500'd the fix at the router). The FRONTEND is covered in the same file deliberately: the store did `data.valid ? 'valid' : 'invalid'`, so a backend-only fix would have turned a false green into a false RED - a tamper alarm for a merely-unhashed log. Pins the tri-state branch, the new store state, the removal of the store's own vacuous 'valid' for an empty list (asserted client-side without even calling the API), and an amber badge so the state does not fall through to 'Verify failed'. Source assertions strip // comments before matching - the inverse of the #1941 trap, since this fix's own comments quote the old code while explaining why it went.

Scheduler execution-origin attribution (#1970). schedule_executions has carried five source_* audit columns since AUDIT-001 and the backend populates them everywhere it owns, but the scheduler is a separate service whose create_execution() omitted them from the INSERT and had no parameter to receive them - so every scheduler-created row was written with all five NULL (observed across 100+ runs). triggered_by='manual' recorded THAT a human ran something, never who; the attribution survived only in logs, bounded by log retention. Not a vulnerability - nothing authorizes on these columns. Covers: the INSERT persists all five and the returned ScheduleExecution mirrors the row (a caller acting on the model would otherwise still see the bug); a cron tick stays NULL (inventing an owner for a caller-less run is worse than an honest blank); every parameter stays keyword-optional so an un-migrated call site still inserts; partial origin accepted (a webhook has no user, a UI click no MCP key). Boundary parse of the untrusted trigger body: exact backend field names (a rename on either side silently restores the NULLs with no error), malformed/legacy/absent bodies degrade to empty origin rather than failing the run, non-int source_user_id DROPPED not coerced (bool IS an int in Python, so True would persist as real user 1), strings length-capped, blank -> None so empty-string and NULL are not two spellings of unknown. Non-cron paths the DB fix alone would leave blank: a retry inherits the original execution's origin (else attempt 1 is the only attributable attempt) and a reminder inherits the provenance #1296 already stored, with the mapper tolerating a table predating those columns. Plus the hop where the identity was actually dropped - the backend's delegating POST sent no body at all - the validated current_user.agent_name preferred over the raw X-Source-Agent header when absent, the MCP third surface (Invariant #13) sending the origin headers, and a guard that the generic extraHeaders hook cannot replace the bearer token.

/edge-cases boundary + property analysis of ExecutionOrigin.from_payload (#1970) - the validation boundary for the scheduler's unauthenticated manual-trigger endpoint, whose parsed output is written straight into five audit columns. 31 enumerated boundary rows (non-dict bodies, string trim/cap/blank/'0', user_id type partitions incl. the bool-is-int trap, int64 limits) plus 6 Hypothesis properties (total function, output types match the columns, strings stripped+capped+never-blank, is_empty agrees with the fields, parsing idempotent and non-mutating). Found TWO real bugs, both fixed in the same change: (1) from_payload bounded TYPE and string LENGTH but not RANGE, so an out-of-int64 source_user_id reached the INSERT and raised OverflowError (SQLite raises rather than truncating) - on the #1970 path that lands in a blanket except AFTER the endpoint already answered 'triggered', silently losing the run; (2) is_empty() tested truthiness where it meant 'is not None', so user_id=0 read as no attribution at all (Hypothesis-shrunk to {'source_user_id': 0}) - latent, since nothing in src/ called it yet, which is precisely why it was worth fixing before the first caller inherited a helper that lies. Both bugs lived inside code that already had 100% statement AND branch coverage from test_1970_execution_origin.py: full coverage says every line ran, not that every value class was tried.

POST /api/settings/ops/reset writes an audit entry (#1966). ent#297 / PR #1893 added validation AND an audit entry to PUT /api/settings/ops/config, and its own prose claimed the audit half covered both routes ('neither this endpoint nor /ops/reset logged anything') - but /ops/reset never got one, so the exact asymmetry ent#297 objected to survived one route over: the generic PUT /{key} audits, /ops/config audits, /ops/reset (admin-only, deletes a row per key in OPS_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS) left no trace. The retention half of that prose does hold - reset continues over RETENTION_OPS_KEYS (#1638) - so what could silently revert unlogged was everything else, including ssh_access_enabled, which decides whether ephemeral SSH credentials can be minted at all. Covers: the handler emits exactly one CONFIGURATION entry with action ops_settings_reset (asserted against the handler's OWN source slice, since /ops/config's ops_settings_change sits ~30 lines up and a whole-file grep would pass on it) carrying actor_ip/endpoint/request_id; the action name is DISTINCT from ops_settings_change, because setting values and deleting rows are different acts and sharing a name would make them indistinguishable in the very log built to tell them apart; details name which keys were reset, cover ssh_access_enabled specifically, and carry keys+counts only (no values - they are being deleted); retention keys appear under skipped and NEVER under reset, with a direct assertion that they were not actually deleted either (a #1638 regression guard); and the entry is written even when nothing was stored - gating on `deleted` the way /ops/config gates on `updated` would make 'reset, nothing to do' indistinguishable from 'never attempted', which is this issue's own reporting gap in miniature. Two tests document the coupling the handler leans on: the log call sits inside the try that maps to a 500 with no guard of its own, which is safe ONLY because platform_audit_service.log swallows its own failures - pinned at the service's source via its db.create_audit_entry seam rather than taken on faith from a docstring. Mirrors test_297_ops_settings_validation.py's harness, including the _Admin dataclass (a bare MagicMock has a truthy .agent_name and would exercise the agent-key branch, the #1816 trap re-hit in ent#293).

The agent server was outside ent#314's YAML sweep (#1965). utils/safe_yaml.py (PR #1961) put every author-controlled YAML reader in the backend behind one hardened loader, and its AST guard walks the whole backend with an EMPTY allowlist - but it walked _BACKEND.rglob only, so docker/base-image/agent_server/ kept six bare yaml.safe_load calls on documents the backend itself assigns REJECT: template.yaml (x2, credential_requirements_service), skill frontmatter (skill_packaging), dashboard.yaml (compatibility/static_checks) and .trinity/persistent-state.yaml. The vector is amplification at SERIALIZATION, not parse - a 416 B level-6 anchor bomb resolves in ~0.001 s and blows up to ~110 MB when something walks the graph - and the backend proxies /info and /dashboard, so the walk happens in-container then again across the wire. Covers: byte-parity of the vendored loader (the credential_paths.py shape, Invariant #5) plus proof the vendored COPY actually behaves - refuses a level-6 bomb under BUDGET, any alias under REJECT, duplicate keys, and still parses an honest document (byte parity is not behaviour parity if the file never imports); each of the four agent-authored sites on the shared loader with its backend counterpart's kind AND policy; /config/agent-config.yaml deliberately BUDGET not REJECT, stated as an exception because the platform writes it and bind-mounts it mode:'ro' so the agent cannot author it, and yaml.dump emits an anchor for any shared object reference - REJECT there would be a self-inflicted outage for no security; no bare safe_load left anywhere in the tree; and HardenedYamlError named in the except arms that previously caught only yaml.YAMLError (it is a ValueError, so without its own arm a refused bomb escapes to the generic handler and surfaces as the unnamed 500 the AC rules out - the trap static_checks._parse_yaml records backend-side). AC #4 end-to-end: a level-6 bomb in a container's template.yaml is refused by BOTH template.yaml readers with the expanded graph never reaching the response, an honest template still serves, and the metrics assertion checks the NAMED refusal rather than has_metrics:False - a bomb parses fine under bare safe_load and yields no metrics: key, so the flag alone passes against the very tree this issue reports. The AST-guard widening itself lives in test_ent314_hardened_yaml.py (both trees, still empty allowlist) rather than here, because splitting a guard across two files is how the second copy stops being run.

Multi-source skills library (ent#237): the single skills_library_url setting becomes an N-row skill_sources table, one SkillSourceClone per source under /data/skills-library/<id>/. Two properties carry the design decisions. AC#4 custom-wins precedence: resolution is priority ASC then created_at ASC and nothing else encodes it, so the tests assert the ORDER rather than the constants; names stay bare because the agent-side identity IS .claude/skills/<name>/ and both the ent#139 runner and the ent#178 A2A card resolve by bare name; a collision is reported via shadowed_by, never a silent overwrite, and the loser is deliberately not a second list entry. AC#5 tag pinning: test_moved_tag_is_refused_and_payload_never_lands builds the ACTUAL attack (force-moves an upstream tag onto a commit adding an executable) and asserts the payload never reaches disk - asserting only the return value would pass with the working tree already updated; the sibling FRESH-clone test covers the /cso-found bypass where neither the no---force fetch nor the SHA comparison applies because there is no local checkout. Plus: one broken source never blinds the others (a source whose first clone failed has no cwd, which used to 500 the whole merged listing), cache invalidation keyed on every enabled source's commit, legacy adoption consuming skills_library_url so a deleted source is not resurrected (#1638's trap), fresh-install seeding, SSRF/PAT-splice host checks decided by PARSING not substring, and sync-error surfaces carrying no exception text (CodeQL py/stack-trace-exposure). Review round (2026-08-05) adds the three source-lifecycle defects, all one shape - the row moved and the checkout did not: repointing url was a no-op on disk because _update_* fetches origin as written at clone time, so every later sync silently pulled the OLD repo with last_sync_status success while feeding the ent#236 fleet re-inject (asserted on DISK, plus that an UNCHANGED url does not re-clone - a credential-blind compare would re-clone every sync since a private source's on-disk origin carries a PAT the stored URL never does); the documented tag-bump path was unreachable because update_source never cleared last_commit_sha, so v1->v2 compared against v1's SHA and was refused as moved_tag, and on the fresh-clone path that refusal rmtree's first and left the source empty - with the parametrized NEGATIVE that name/enabled/priority must NOT clear the baseline, since a cleared baseline on disable would let a tag moved during the disabled window be adopted silently on re-enable (the AC#5 bypass via a checkbox, and the enabled toggle is the only edit the UI wires to PUT); and delete leaked the checkout, now reclaimed row-first-disk-second with a fail-closed orphan sweep on full syncs only (a sweep reading a DB error as 'no sources' deletes the whole library), scoped to the server-minted id shape so the legacy checkout and operator directories are out of reach, and a disabled source keeping its checkout. The auth guard now matches an ast.Call node rather than 'reject_agent_principal' in ast.dump(fn): ast.dump renders docstrings, so the guard was satisfiable by a comment and passed with the real call deleted - found by mutation-testing it. Both sync routes are in MUTATING and the coverage scan widened from /skills/sources to /skills/, since POST /skills/library/sync sits outside the sources prefix and the old scan reported full coverage while missing it.

Per-source skills-library root (ent#332): catalog.yaml skills_root: declaration -> evidence-gated skills/ probe -> .claude/skills/ fallback, resolved per SkillSourceClone; packaging rewrites tar arcnames to the canonical agent-side .claude/skills/ destination at filter_skill_archive so manifests, prune confinement and the ent#236 removal machinery stay destination-canonical with zero migration. Covers: resolution order + zero-config back-compat; dual-layout (evidence under BOTH roots, no catalog) keeps .claude/skills/ and flags layout_conflict instead of silently flipping which executable content ent#236 auto-injects; segment-wise skills_root validation ('.', './skills', 'skills//x' all rejected -- a whole-string charset regex admits each and breaks archive-prefix math into per-skill empty-package failures); every bad catalog shape (unparseable, alias-bearing HardenedYamlError, non-mapping, unknown schema_version, oversized, symlinked) falls back to probe and never raises through list_skills; symlinked probe/declared roots fall to the next tier rather than blanking the source, and an escaping final tier empty/None-propagates without a TypeError; tree-SHA version parity across layouts (repo restructure with unchanged content keeps versions stable -- no spurious fleet re-inject); arcname rewrite identity for legacy layout, destination-canonical executable_paths, fail-visible layout-mismatch, unsafe source_root ValueError; cross-layout prune continuity; _legacy_fallback SKILL.md lookup with rewritten members; end-to-end mixed-layout merge through the real service with per-source skills_root in library status.

test_ent183_skill_packages wrote fake modules straight into sys.modules at IMPORT time and left them there. That is collection-time code and pytest imports every test module before running a single test, so every file collected afterwards resolved services.settings_service (plus database, services.agent_client, utils.url_validation) to a four-function fake, captured names from it at module scope, and kept those bindings for the session. Its own autouse sys.modules-restore fixture could not help: the damage is a BINDING in another module's namespace, which restoring the module table does not reach. Two symptom shapes, both looking like unrelated bugs - ImportError 'cannot import name X from services.settings_service (unknown location)' at collection (#1855), and silent wrong behaviour when the stub happens to define the name (7 failures in test_1081_physical_meter). Fixed by installing the stubs inside a mock.patch.dict context scoped to the single import that needs them, so nothing survives the with-block while the imported module keeps its stub bindings. Guards the mechanism statically (no module-scope sys.modules assignment - the AST walk deliberately allows assignments inside a with, since banning all of them would ban the fix; and the stubs must sit in a patch.dict) and the outcome behaviourally (a subprocess runs the cheapest known victim after the offender in one process). A first version of the fix also evicted cached services.skill* modules to force a fresh import; that broke 10 sibling tests by producing a second module object, and was reverted - caught by comparing the same selection with and without the change (435 passed without, 10 failed with).

Skills-library status disclosed source repo URLs (ent#334). GET /api/skills/library/status is Depends(get_current_user) - every authenticated caller including agent-scoped MCP keys, deliberately, since the per-agent Skills tab and the MCP get_skills_library_status tool both read it - but it returned skill_service.get_library_status() raw, and that dict carries the source repo URLs: exactly the value GET /api/skills/sources is require_admin PLUS reject_agent_principal to protect (ent#237 classes repo URLs admin-sensitive; ent#293 added the second gate because an agent-scoped key resolves to its owner carrying the owner's role). Two independent failure modes, tested apart because the fixes differ: the URL as a NAME (org/repo discloses what the fleet is taught from - so every route assertion is on KEY ABSENCE, since a 'secret not in body' assertion passes on a payload that still leaks the private repo), and embedded userinfo (reject_embedded_credentials guards only NEW writes; rows predating it and rows from the unvalidated legacy-adoption path still carry https://<token>@host). Covers the new never-raising, parse-based strip_url_credentials - urlparse itself raises ValueError on an unbalanced bracket and the only caller is get_library_status, whose comments say status must never 500 the panel, so the contract is never-raises and the test pins the premise that the input really does raise; scheme-less input, where urlparse('tok@github.com/o/r').username is None so a scheme must be assumed for the PARSE but never invented into the RETURN; userinfo with no host (hostname None, so _replace(netloc=None) would blow up in geturl); empty userinfo, which a parsed.username test reads as falsy; and the double-@ https://a@b@github.com/o/r that BOTH pre-existing scrubbers got wrong ([^@]+@ cannot cross the first @, leaving https://***@b@...). Parse-based, not regex, per skill_service._authenticated_url's house rule that the host is decided by PARSING - a looser pattern mangles a legitimate https://github.com/o/r?ref=a@b where the @ is in the query. The two free-text scrubbers (_scrub_pat, skill_source_clone.redact) stay text-oriented because git stderr carries several URLs and prose, but are widened to [^\s/]+@ so the whole authority goes and an earlier plain URL no longer swallows a later credentialed one (redact's old [^@]+@ crossed / and newlines). Route coverage over a real TestClient rather than a direct handler call, because response_model filtering is applied by FastAPI's serialization layer and a direct call proves nothing about the wire; admin, non-admin and agent-scoped-key-on-an-admin-owned-install callers; that GET /skills/sources still returns the url (narrow the open route, don't blind the operator) and that it is userinfo-free because the strip is at the SERVICE, which is also what stops SkillSourcesPanel.vue rendering a token on the admin route. Plus a static AST guard that the route declares response_model=SkillsLibraryStatus - the allow-list IS the fix, and dropping the decorator kwarg reopens the leak with no behavioural test failing, since the handler's return value is unchanged.

backend-unit-test.yml installs pytest-timeout and never passed --timeout, so one stalled test consumed the whole 25-minute job budget, GitHub cancelled the job, the Upload JUnit XML step was skipped (no if: always()), and the failure read as 'The operation was canceled' against whichever PR was running - four times in one day across all three seeds AND both sides, the base side being plain dev. Guards the fix: a per-test --timeout is present, it is NOT the thread method (thread dumps stacks then kills the process, so the run aborts and the JUnit is incomplete - signal raises inside the test and the suite continues, giving the diff job a complete XML that names the hang as an ordinary new failure), and the value clears the slowest REAL test with room for runner variance. Bounds measured from a green run's JUnit rather than guessed: test_start_agent_skip_inject's two retry cases run ~60.6s, so the 60s the issue originally proposed would have failed them on every PR; a 2.5x-slow runner (the variance that caused #2019) puts them near 150s, hence >=180s, and <=600s so a stall still fails instead of eating the budget. Also pins if: always() on the artifact upload and the load-bearing '|| true' (#660 baseline). Assertions read the step's COMMAND with YAML comments stripped - the step documents its own flags in prose, and an earlier draft passed with '|| true' deleted because the comment still mentioned it (the #1871/ent#314 textual-scan trap, third occurrence). The step slice is indentation-bounded after a name-bounded version ran past the last step and matched the diff job's own 'if: always()'.

_patch_env_github_pat replaced only the FIRST matching line (count=1) while the agent's own .env reader is LAST-WINS, so on a file carrying a duplicate GITHUB_PAT line the rotation wrote the new token to line 1, the revoked token survived below it, and the agent kept authenticating with the revoked one - while propagate_pat_to_all_agents reported that agent as 'updated'. Same silent-success class #1967 exists to close, reached differently: there the rotation never touched the agent, here it touches it and the agent ignores the result. The duplicate is not created by this function (it appends only when the key is absent) - it arrives from an agent editing its own .env (#1999), an SSH/docker-exec append, or a restored file. Fixed by dropping the cap so every occurrence is levelled; NOT de-duplicated, since after levelling every copy carries the same value and removing lines would be a second behaviour change for no correctness gain. Every assertion goes through what the AGENT READS rather than what the file contains - the file did contain the new token, on a line nothing read. Covers the reproduction, the revoked token surviving nowhere in the file (shells and greps read .env too), 2/3/5 copies, each of the three #1574 mirrored keys independently (each runs its own substitution, so a cap left on one reopens the bug for that key), interleaved duplicates of different keys, the messy real-world duplicate shapes (indented/tabbed/unquoted/single-quoted/empty-value), a commented duplicate deliberately left alone, lookalike keys untouched, and the single-line path unchanged incl. idempotence. Structural guard reads the CALL via ast, not the source text: this function's docstring explains the bug and therefore contains the string 'count=1', so a textual scan passes on the prose with the cap restored (the #1871/ent#314 trap; the first draft of this test failed exactly that way). Mutation-verified against BOTH spellings - count=1 and the positional third argument - 15 of 21 fail on each.

Claude Code's internal [ede_diagnostic] header must never be surfaced as the error cause (#1849): stream_parser filters diagnostic entries from result.errors at BOTH the max_turns and execution_error branches, joins the remaining real errors, keeps the token-stripped diagnostic payload as labelled context, and no longer raises on a malformed errors shape (which previously landed as HTTP 200 success). Acceptance test drives a marker-first errors[] through _finalize_headless_result to routers/sessions.py::_is_resume_not_found.

Two edge cases in ask_trinity (ent#328/#1981), found by /edge-cases. (1) truncate cut on UTF-16 CODE UNITS, so a boundary landing inside a surrogate pair left an unpaired surrogate - ill-formed Unicode that a strict UTF-8 encoder or JSON-RPC client replaces with U+FFFD or rejects; proven by construction (65,536-char answer with U+1F600 straddling the cut). Fixed by stepping back one unit off a high surrogate; only the final unit can be orphaned, so one check covers it. (2) The context-loss warning lived inside `if (responseSessionId)`, so a 200 that answered but OMITTED session_id produced no warning at all and the caller silently lost its conversation context - exactly what that warning exists to prevent; the 'different id returned' branch was covered and the neighbouring 'no id returned' one was not. The warning is now decided by the REQUEST's session, with distinct wording since 'a new session was started' is false when none came back. Both fixes are mirrored into src/helper-mcp/src/client.ts, which carries a byte-identical copy. Covers: the straddling cut, the limit still reported as the ORIGINAL max, a fully-fitting pair surviving, a BMP-only answer still cut at exactly max (the step-back must not misfire), a short answer untouched, the 200-char ERROR-path truncation (likelier to meet arbitrary bytes than the answer path), and all four session shapes. Two rows were also added to the existing PARITY_CASES table: mutating ONLY the helper copy previously changed nothing in the suite - the parity claim held just for the cases in its table - and both helper-only mutations now fail it.

deploy-local validated an archive-supplied .mcp.json 32 lines AFTER shutil.copytree(extract_root, dest_path), and the finally block removed only temp_dir - so a config the ent#213 validator refused stayed on disk under /data/deployed-templates/<version_name>/, a live member of crud._LOCAL_TEMPLATE_ROOTS, addressable by the same caller via POST /api/agents {template: local:<version_name>}. A guard that runs after the persist is not a gate. Fix: the guard moved to step 6a, running on extract_root before the copy AND before the quota check and the stop-previous-version step (a doomed deploy no longer stops a running agent on its way to a 400), plus _remove_partial_deploy as a second layer for failures between copytree and create_agent_fn (_prepopulate_workspace_from_template's 500) - deliberately handed over before creation starts, since a directory a container may already reference must not be removed on a late failure. ent#213's suite tests _validate_archive_mcp_config in isolation ('the full deploy flow needs Docker'), which is exactly why the ordering was never covered; these drive the REAL deploy_local_agent_logic and assert on the filesystem, needing no Docker because the rejection path now reaches nothing external. Covers: the issue's reproduction, local:<name> resolving to nothing, the ordering pinned twice (behaviourally by exploding every post-guard step, and statically by source order - the behavioural residue assertion alone cannot distinguish the two candidate fixes once cleanup exists), the valid path reaching creation with the template in place, an archive with no .mcp.json, and both sides of the cleanup boundary.

PULL_MODE_PILOT_AGENTS can only route agent-to-agent work (#2048). _AUTONOMOUS_TRIGGERS declares seven triggers autonomous and pull_owns_dispatch consulted all seven, but capacity_manager only offers a row to the durable queue when its producer passed overflow_policy='queue_persistent', and exactly one of the three producers does: task_execution_service uses 'reject' (scheduler/ALL cron + fan-out), dispatch_admission_service uses 'queue_in_memory' (sequential chat, human chat), only chat_execution_service (POST /task) uses 'queue_persistent'. So on a cron-driven agent the pilot flag is INERT and #1766's soak measures nothing - silently, because the gate sits behind an overflow_policy short-circuit, so for a schedule row pull_owns_dispatch is never called at all and the row is pushed indistinguishably from the flag being unset, while PULL_MIGRATION_TESTING.md section 9 M1 told the operator to go check an env var that is present and correct. Issue decision was Option 1 (make the reach honest, do not extend it). Corrects the issue's own table: the reachable set is {agent, event}, not {agent} - #1578's task-completion loopback POSTs to the same /task route and is tagged 'event' via an internal-secret-gated X-Event-Trigger, with no capacity bypass. Tests pin: the reach set derived from what _derive_task_trigger can emit rather than hardcoded; every autonomous trigger classified as reachable or stranded so a new one cannot join the stranded set unreviewed; the narrowing is a runtime NO-OP over the only producer that consults the predicate (it stops a false claim, it does not change a verdict); and note_unreachable_pull_trigger reports a stranded row once per (agent, trigger), never for a non-pilot / reachable / interactive trigger, and never raises. A structural guard asserts the three producers' overflow_policy literals, so implementing the deferred Option 2 (wiring cron to queue_persistent) fails this test and forces PULL_REACHABLE_TRIGGERS and section 9's prose to be revisited in the same change - a silently-stale reach set being exactly the bug. Also updates test_1766: its 'pilot owns EVERY autonomous trigger' case asserted reach the system never had (it passed only by calling the predicate outside the context that constrains it), and its producer-gate case drove a queue_persistent acquire carrying 'schedule' - a combination production cannot produce - now driven with 'agent', the shape that actually occurs.

The free-text PAT scrubbers only fired on a literal `https://` (#2052) - the follow-up ent#347 predicted. `skill_source_clone._CREDENTIAL_URL_RE` was `https://[^\s/?#]+@`, anchored on the scheme, while the parse-based `utils.url_validation.strip_url_credentials` (ent#334) resolves an authority with no scheme at all. Three shapes therefore slipped past the regex and were echoed VERBATIM: protocol-relative `//tok@github.com/o/r`, the scheme-less shorthand `tok@github.com/o/r`, and an alternate scheme `git+ssh://tok@...` (plus the empty-userinfo `https://@host`, which the old `+` quantifier could not match). Reachable rather than theoretical: `_adopt_legacy_clone` writes source rows with no validation and `validate_skills_library_url` accepts the scheme-less form, so a stored URL may legitimately take them, and `_scrub_pat` then runs over `str(e)` of an ARBITRARY exception whose text is not constrained to what `_authenticated_url` built. Sink is `system_settings['skills_library_last_error']` - durable and admin-rendered. Fixed by moving the rule next to the parser as `scrub_url_credentials_in_text` rather than adding a fourth hand-written regex; `redact` delegates and `_CREDENTIAL_URL_RE` is deleted. The free-text side stays text-oriented on purpose - git stderr is prose plus several URLs, so there is no single URL to hand `urlparse`. Tests are mostly PARITY assertions over one shared corpus (the ent#334 cross-check shapes plus the three that regressed): the two must agree on the resolved authority, on WHETHER a credential is present at all (the actual defect), and no userinfo may survive. A structural test asserts `_CREDENTIAL_URL_RE` is gone so a local pattern cannot be reintroduced. Regression guards keep `?ref=a@b` untouched - the removed scheme anchor was also what kept the pattern off a query `@`, which is why the bare form carries a run-start boundary - plus multi-URL free text, idempotency and never-raises. 21 of these fail against the pre-fix scrubber, one with the token verbatim. Also pins the scan LINEAR: dropping the `https://` anchor also drops the literal `str.find` could jump to, and the first fix expressed the new rule as a class-first pattern, which rescanned a long no-`@` run from every offset - 24s on 200KB, 151s on 500KB, on RAW git stderr that is unbounded and partly remote-controlled, i.e. a DoS reachable from a hostile repo. Rewritten to walk maximal authority-legal runs; same 500KB now scrubs in 1.2ms.

TZ-capability packaging parity (#1823), #1891-shaped static guard. Both tz-resolving images (backend, scheduler) install `tzdata-legacy` AND declare the `tzdata` wheel; tests/requirements-test.txt declares it too (CI must not be MORE capable than production — that inversion kept this bug green on CI and red in the image for months); the base image's exemption is asserted against the reason that holds (its tree registers no CronTrigger) rather than inherited; and both images pin the SAME APScheduler exactly, since the #1472 contract ('reject exactly what the scheduler would') is only true while validator and executor build the same CronTrigger — a floor on either side does not merely risk drift, it produces it, as `>=3.10.0,<4.0.0` resolves to whatever is newest at build time. The pure registry.yaml parser (ent#14 / TMPL-002). Covers the happy path; `templates: []` treated as a SUCCESS rather than a failure, because an empty registry is the deliberate day-one state and classifying it as an error would serve stale entries forever; every document-level refusal; ent#314 YAML hardening reaching this document specifically (any single alias, a level-6 anchor bomb, duplicate keys, oversize - all refuse the WHOLE document and degrade to the bundled floor, never a partial parse); per-entry drops; dot path segments; case-insensitive duplicate repos; field caps; `priority: true` not sorting as 1 (a bool is an int in Python and used to 500 the router's sort); a bounded error list; and THE ALLOWLIST - 16 forbidden keys asserted absent from the frozen four-field record, so a hostile registry cannot inject fork_to_own, credentials, schedules, data_paths, persistent_state, skills, hidden or id.

Transport + cache for the remote registry (ent#14). The byte ceiling counts WIRE bytes via iter_raw (S1): a gzip bomb whose Content-Length passes the early abort is refused as encoding_refused with zero body bytes read, and peak allocation is asserted under 8 MB against 64 MB of decoded payload. Both transport fixtures convert every mock response to a REAL stream - a buffered httpx.Response(content=...) decodes in its constructor and marks the stream consumed, so it can only ever exercise iter_bytes(), which is precisely why the pre-S1 ceiling tests were green against a 1030:1 hole. Also: a LYING Content-Length re-probed through a second client to prove the lie was actually told (otherwise a future refactor that starts trusting the header stays green); early abort on a declared oversize length; connect/timeout/HTTP/redirect failures; HTML and binary bodies; URL-validation refusal never dialling; TTL + jitter; URL change; the cross-worker GENERATION bump (a per-process invalidate half-applies under --workers 2); serve-stale and its 7-day cap; negative caching; and the durable last-known-good (persist-on-change-only, cold-start restore, and rejection of a wrong-URL / older-parser / too-old / tampered row).

The fail-open MATRIX at the catalog seam (ent#14). The design rule is that a broken registry can only ever degrade to the bundled floor, never break the catalog - so every assertion is on the CATALOG OUTPUT, not on whether an except branch ran (a test asserting the branch ran still passes if the branch returns garbage). 19 failure modes x 2: catalog equality, and again through the ROUTER's own sort, where a non-int priority used to 500 the endpoint. Plus a registry service that simply RAISES; per-entry fencing; the full precedence ladder admin-override -> registry -> DEFAULT_GITHUB_TEMPLATE_REPOS including zero-requests-when-curated; the config hard kill switch beating the DB row; list/detail/create sharing ONE ladder (F1 - the second resolver feeds GET /api/templates/{id} AND agent creation, so a divergence changes what gets cloned); payload key-set equality; and a hostile registry failing to inject fork_to_own / credentials / schedules / hidden / id. GET/PUT/DELETE /api/settings/template-registry on the real router (ent#14). All four owner/repo gates agree on a shared fixture corpus (ent#14). Compares BEHAVIOUR, not source strings - two of the copies already differ in character-class ordering, so a source diff would report drift that does not exist and miss drift that does. The fork_to_own fail-closed gate (ent#14 F2 + S2). F2: a rate-limited (403) template.yaml read as fork_to_own=None skipped the gate and bound the agent to the SHARED upstream template repo instead of a user-owned copy. S2 is the sharper case - the gate decided from the CATALOG dict (global platform PAT, default branch, 600s process cache) while the correctly-credentialed creation read ran one line earlier. That failed in both directions at once: GitHub answers 404 (not 403) for a repo a token cannot see, so a PRIVATE fork_to_own: required template readable only by the creator's per-user PAT (ent#162, a supported flow) came back absent and the gate PASSED (false pass, no attacker involved); and a poisoned shared cache entry 503'd creators whose own PAT reads fine for the full TTL (false refuse). Driven through the REAL _resolve_template against a GitHub whose answer depends on which token asks. Verified red (measured 2026-08-05): neutralising the F2 guard fails 11 of 31; restoring the catalog-reading gate fails 3; and the plausible HALF-FIX - moving only the availability verdict while the value still comes from the catalog - still fails 1, so the suite is not vacuous against the fix that tests green.

SSRF gate on the template-registry URL (ent#14 S3): RFC 6598 shared address space (100.64.0.0/10) is reported by Python's ipaddress as neither is_private nor is_reserved, so the predicate stack admitted it — refused now, with both /10 boundaries held public so a legitimate registry is not blackholed, and one CGNAT record among public ones enough to refuse (every resolved record is checked). Also pins WHY the sibling validate_skills_library_url has no CGNAT clause and must not grow one as a consistency fix: it is allowlisted by HOST, so the operator never chooses a destination and the resolved address is not an operator-controlled input. Four non-allowlisted hosts (incl. the suffix lookalike github.com.evil.com and the real-but-unlisted raw.githubusercontent.com) are refused while resolving to a PUBLIC address, so the refusal provably does not come from the address predicates, plus the accept case so it is an allowlist and not a blanket refusal. Compose/env packaging for the two registry knobs (ent#14), caught by /validate-pr before merge. config.py read TEMPLATE_REGISTRY_ENABLED / TEMPLATE_REGISTRY_URL and NEITHER compose file injected them; prod compose launches standalone (no base merge, no env_file) and is what every deploy path uses, so both were inert on any real instance. Sixth recurrence of the #1039/#1056 packaging-gap class (after #1056 VOIP_*, ent#31 LOG_*, #1039, #1871 AGENT_LOG_*, #411 CANARY_*), so it is pinned rather than trusted. Shape mirrors test_canary_env_prod_parity.py, the guard for the fifth. The meta-test proves the matcher fails on pre-fix content AND on a hardcoded value; the guard was additionally verified by deleting the real prod line and watching it go red - the first attempt at that proof used an unescaped grep -v whose $ read as an end-of-line anchor, matched nothing, and reported a false green.

The .trinity/ authored-vs-runtime split survives a backend Push (#2070). Every Push runs `git rm --cached` over tracked-but-now-ignored files; the fleet list ignored `.trinity/` WHOLESALE, so template-committed content there was untracked and its deletion pushed, guarded only by a hardcoded two-entry pathspec that was wrong three times (brain-orb ent#76, setup.sh — swept live — and pre-check #2070, the SCHED-COND-001 hook the platform's own docs tell authors to commit). Silent by construction: only the index is touched, so the working tree keeps running and the failure lands one re-clone/recreate later as an agent with no hook, whose every cron tick then runs a full LLM turn. Runs the REAL `_build_gitignore_merge_command` + `_build_rm_cached_ignored_command` against REAL git repos in tmp (the defect is in git's own descend/negation semantics, which a mocked container cannot express). Asserts the SPLIT, never the current exemption strings: 8 authored paths survive, 9 runtime files stay untracked, a fresh clone still RUNS the hook, the superseded wholesale line is replaced (append-only would be inert — git never descends into a dir-form exclusion), user rules merely mentioning .trinity are preserved, the merge is idempotent, exemptions are derived from `_TRINITY_AUTHORED_PATHS`, and a newly-invented runtime file needs no action. Mutation-verified 4 ways (wholesale ignore restored 5F, hardcoded exemptions 1F, no stale-line migration 2F, pre-check dropped from the set 4F).

The fleet-wide `.gitignore` merge now runs at agent CREATION (#2069). `_GITIGNORE_PATTERNS` was applied only on Push/init, never at creation, so a `github:` agent whose 15-min in-container auto-sync loop is on from birth (the GIT_SYNC_AUTO set — non-source/fork agents, ephemeral ghosts INCLUDED) auto-committed `.trinity/` runtime state and the root-level `.env`/`.mcp.json` into its user-owned repo before any Push could migrate the list. Loads the REAL git_service (heavy deps mocked) through crud.git_service so the predicate, merge builders and readiness poller are production code. (1) Merge behaviour (AC#2): the real `_build_gitignore_merge_command` output run against real tmp git repos — no-.gitignore template gets the full list, a partial one is preserved+completed, and after the merge a bare `git add -A` stages NONE of .env/.mcp.json/.trinity/*/content/*/.claude/projects while genuine code + the .gitignore itself ARE staged; #2070 authored hooks (.trinity/pre-check) stay includable. (2) Idempotence/#953 (AC#4): an EXACT-seed template committed to a bare origin shows no `M .gitignore`; run-twice is a no-op (no pattern duplicated); a stale wholesale `.trinity/` line yields a LEGITIMATE supersede→append edit (#2070) — proving the no-drift contract is scoped to already-canonical templates. (3) Readiness gating (AC#1/R1): merge_gitignore_after_clone waits while /health is down and times out cleanly with no exception; once ready ∧ .git present it runs `_build_gitignore_merge_command` against the toplevel and NEVER `_build_rm_cached_ignored_command` (creation is PREVENT, not REMEDIATE); skips a ready-but-no-.git failed clone and an unresolved `_git_toplevel` None; and a hung docker exec is `asyncio.wait_for`-bounded (a missing wrap would hang the test); and the readiness poll runs OUTSIDE `_gitignore_merge_semaphore` so a slow-/never-booting agent parked in its /health wait cannot head-of-line-block a healthy already-ready agent's Docker-exec merge — pinned with a 1-permit semaphore, since the pre-fix in-semaphore poll would deadlock the fast agent. (4) `_git_auto_sync_baked` matrix (R2): fork-to-own AND non-source AND ephemeral non-source github+PAT bake (the ghost is never operator-Pushed, so the merge MUST cover it — the predicate ignores config.ephemeral), while source-mode-non-fork, local/no-repo, no-PAT and ephemeral-source-mode do NOT — and `_materialize_agent_files` fires spawn_gitignore_merge_after_clone on EXACTLY that predicate (the AC#6 regression, real predicate flowing through crud). (5) Start/recreate wiring (T1): an AST structural guard that start_agent_internal fires the spawn gated on db.get_git_auto_sync_enabled and NOWHERE ungated (fleet remediation for existing leakers; ghosts never recreate so the DB flag is complete). No Docker, no live backend, no Redis.

AST writer-SET guard that `_GITIGNORE_PATTERNS` stays the single source of truth (#2069 AC#3 / R4, the test_ent109_git_env_seam precedent). Guards the full-suite harness against silently rotting back (#2080). Every defect that issue fixed removed COVERAGE without failing anything: collection aborted before any test ran, tiers skipped themselves, and a sys.modules shadow swallowed each new src/backend/utils module. Asserts: tests/utils cannot come back (it shadowed the backend package on the pythonpath — adding safe_yaml.py broke ~1,000 tests with a ModuleNotFoundError that read like a product regression) and no test imports the helpers under the old name; no package directory has a non-identifier name (tests/git-sync's __init__.py put its conftest under the bare `conftest` key and collided with the root one, breaking collection of tests/integration and aborting the run before the unit tier); every test directory is named by a tier in run-full.sh; every tier passes -rs (without it the skip audit is blind) and a thread-method timeout; pytest exit code 5 (no tests collected) is a FAILURE; pyproject pins timeout_method=thread for hand-run pytest. Plus the audit's own honesty: each allowlist entry carries a written justification, an empty log dir refuses to certify, an unallowlisted skip fails and an allowlisted one passes.

Pins that the workspace / client portal stays OSS core (ent#356).
